items.title: Michael Abene interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 11, 2003
items.q: the only reason we moved is my sister and her family decided to move... the band director was a man by the name of Marshall Brown who was probably one of the foremost beginning of the jazz educators along with people like Clem DeRosa and the John LaPortas and others on the east coast

ctx.x: Was living in New York — this is probably a yes — a positive place to be for your craft?

Well I was born in Brooklyn, New York and then when I was about I think 12 years old we moved out to Farmingdale, Long Island which is a very important part, because, and the only reason we moved is my sister and her family decided to move and the Italian thing is you know your kids go there, you got to go, you can’t, it’s not like you are oceans away. So we wound up on Long Island of course now what a drag, I’m trying to play. So I was in a school called Farmingdale High School and the band director was a man by…

original, and I started writing for the band at one point. So it was a wonderful experience, also learning how to rehearse a band too. Again John LaPorta and Lou Mucci would come in and rehearse, tutor the band, in phrasing, so you talk about jazz education, my God. So to this day I feel I have, and Jimmy Owens, we’ve always discussed this, about how to rehearse a band and how to deal with students. We feel we’ve had an advantage you know, kind of making it fun and Marshall was brilliant in the sense that he knew…
